svg.aria-label: Fig 5. Planned code lookups. A card catalog has drawers for HCPCS Level II, ICD-10-CM, CARC and RARC values, and a locked CPT drawer marked not used. An agent asks for CARC 197, the catalog answers CARC 197: prior_auth, and a green track takes the answer to a check with format rows for each code set and a red row that rejects CPT.
svg.title: Fig 5. Planned code lookups. A card catalog has drawers for HCPCS Level II, ICD-10-CM, CARC and RARC values, and a locked CPT drawer marked not used. An agent asks for CARC 197, the catalog answers CARC 197: prior_auth, and a green track takes the answer to a check with format rows for each code set and a red row that rejects CPT.
svg.text: Code values only. No CPT. Planned design, not built.
agents pick codes from the catalog only
1 The catalog holds small public subsets: HCPCS Level II (CMS) and ICD-10-CM (CDC/NCHS),
with attribution. CARC and RARC hold code values with our own labels, not X12 text.
The CPT drawer stays locked. We use no CPT codes or descriptors, and no AMA license (D-009).
2 An agent asks for a code value. Example: CARC 197 from the adjustment CO-197 (group code CO).
3 The catalog returns the value and our own category label (example: prior_auth).
4 A check confirms that every code is in the catalog and matches its format.
No free-text codes go into a claim, a prompt or a letter.
black: 1 to 2 (the agent uses the catalog) and 2 to 3 (the lookup). green: 3 to 4 (the answer is checked).
ICD-10-CM: LETTER, DIGIT, UP TO 5 MORE
RARC: M, MA OR N + DIGITS
